packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-07 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context proposed an identification of these fragments or a reading
of them. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..015 of this packet (plus the reader
brief). No web, no search, no packet.json. I do not name a work or author below.
One thing beyond a plain viewing: because several fragments are mounted sideways, I
made rotated and enlarged working copies of image-002, -005, -007, -010, -012 and
-015 in my own scratch directory (not under /tmp/frag12d) so the text could be read
upright. No other processing; nothing else was opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
The images show a bound book with parchment manuscript waste reused as spine
linings; the pieces wrap round the spine and their ends are pasted onto the inside
of both boards/pastedowns. Three views:
- image-001 (overview): inside of one board, book lying sideways, colour chart
  alongside. Four parchment tabs along the joint. Tiles: image-002 (tab 1), 003
  (tab 2), 004 (tab 3), 005 (tab 4).
- image-006 (overview): inside of the other board. Four tabs. Tiles: image-007
  (tab 1), 008 (tab 2), 009 (tab 3), 010 (tab 4).
- image-011 (overview): the bare spine, with four lining panels between the sewing
  supports and the red/yellow endbands. Tiles: image-012 (panel 1), 013 (panel 2),
  014 (panel 3), 015 (panel 4).
Each lining piece is therefore seen in three parts (tab - spine panel - tab), and
the three parts of one piece are continuous lines of text interrupted by the turns
over the joints, where some letters are hidden.

Two different source manuscripts appear to be involved (observation of script and
size, not an inference about works):
(A) LARGE-SCRIPT pieces = tabs/panels 2 and 3: a large formal book hand, widely
    spaced lines (about 8-9 mm line pitch by the chart), text upright relative to
    the book's spine. Little abbreviation; nomina-sacra-style contractions with
    horizontal strokes (n with stroke + ro; s-c-u with stroke). Punctuation by
    point and by punctus elevatus-like mark. No rubric or initial visible. Each
    piece gives only a few letters or words from the middle of 3-5 lines.
(B) SMALL-SCRIPT pieces = tabs/panels 1 and 4: a small compressed gothic book hand
    written at right angles to the large-script pieces (lines run parallel to the
    spine). Heavily abbreviated. Red ink is visible on the spine panel 1 (image-012,
    near the left edge in the original orientation: a red paraph or initial stroke)
    and a thin red line on panel 4 (image-015). A tall capital with pen flourish
    occurs twice on tab 1 (image-002). No running title, no gloss layout visible.
    The crops are too tight to say whether this was one or two columns.
Tab 3 on the second board (image-009) is abraded to bare skin; only ink specks.

SPANS SELECTED
1. Large-script piece "3" across image-004, image-014 (best preserved; 5 lines).
2. Large-script piece "2" across image-003, image-013, image-008.
3. Small-script piece "1": image-002, image-007, image-012.
Unread or nearly so: image-009 (abraded), image-005 / -010 / -015 (piece 4, only a
few letters per line), and the parts of piece 1 lying in the folds of the joint
(image-007 lower/left edge, where further lines are visible edge-on).

TRANSCRIPTION

--- (A) Large-script piece 3 ---
Tab on first board, image-004 (lines from top of image; the piece starts at the
third visible line group; left edge cut, right edge runs into the joint):
image-004 l.1  [bottoms of letters only] ]um(?) [..]mi[..](?)
image-004 l.2  ]e(m)(?) n(oste)r oratio[        (written: e with stroke, "nr" with stroke, "oratio")
image-004 l.3  ]us : et oste[                   (a stroke over the final "e": oste(n)[ ?)
image-004 l.4  ]per s(an)c(t)uariu[             (written "scuariu" with stroke over "cu")
image-004 l.5  ]um est . p(ro)p[                (last letters at the edge: p with a
               crossed descender, then one or two more minims/letters going into the joint)
(image-005 l.1 repeats image-004 l.5: overlap.)

Spine panel of the same piece, image-014 (lines from top of that image; surface
flaked in vertical strips):
image-014 l.1  ][..]un(?)de(?) ag[              (tops of letters lost; uncertain)
image-014 l.2  ]n(?) fes[.] tu[                 (gap in the middle from loss)
image-014 l.3  ] de fa[.]ie[                    (third letter of second word lost in a flake; "facie"?)
image-014 l.4  ] tuam(?) [..] qui(?)[           (first word: "tuam" or "-buam"; second begins q/p)
image-014 l.5  ]pter temetip[                   (i.e. the line ends in the joint after "temetip")
I cannot prove from the images how image-004 lines pair with image-014 lines, but
both show five lines at the same pitch, and image-004 l.5 "...est . p(ro)p" followed
across the joint by image-014 l.5 "pter temetip" looks like one continuous line
(observation: "p(ro)p|pter" would need the joint to hide or double a syllable, so
the join is approximate).

Tab of piece 3 on the second board, image-009: abraded; scattered ink remains of
about five lines, no letter legible.

--- (A) Large-script piece 2 ---
Tab on first board, image-003 (lines from top; ignore the sideways small-script
tab at the very top of the tile, which is tab 1 again):
image-003 l.1  ][.]um(?)                       (tops lost; minims with a final m)
image-003 l.2  ]n   n(ost)ro[                  ("nro" with stroke; wide space before it)
image-003 l.3  ] obp(ro)briu[                  (p with crossed descender; ends at the joint)
image-003 l.4  [tops of letters only] ][..]m(?) [..]m[..](?)
(image-004 top edge repeats image-003 l.3-4: overlap.)

Spine panel, image-013 (lines from top of the large-script panel):
image-013 l.1  ][.]u(?) n(ost)ra(m)(?) . et uu[   (first word: minims + "a" with strokes above;
               after the point "et" then "uu"/"vu" and a lost letter)
image-013 l.2  ](m)(?) hier(usa)l(e)m et [        (written "hierl" with abbreviation marks; preceded
               by a letter with a stroke, at the edge)
image-013 l.3  ]um  fuit om(n)ib[                 (stroke over "om"; ends "ib" + minims)
image-013 l.4  [tops only; a round capital-like form at the left] ]D(?)[..]
Reading across the joint, image-013 l.3 "...fuit omnib[us]" would be followed on
the tab by image-003 l.3 "... obprobriu[m]" or the reverse; I cannot determine the
order of tab and panel from the images alone (it depends on which board is the
front), so I leave the two parts separate.

Tab on second board, image-008 (lines from top of the large-script tab; a strip of
the same lines continues on the spine edge at left):
image-008 l.1  ][.]as(?)   p(ro)(?)[            (very rubbed; "p" with a crossed descender, then cut)
image-008 l.2  [edge: t] ][..]a(?)  uiui[       (after "uiui" a tall letter: l, s or f)
image-008 l.3  [edge: m(?)] ]  [.]arui[ / [.]anni[   (first letter rubbed: p? ; "parui" or "anni")
image-008 l.4  [a single descender/stroke only]

--- (B) Small-script piece 1 ---
All lines below are read with the tile turned 90 degrees counter-clockwise (i.e.
the text runs up the page in the supplied images). Line numbers are counted from
the top of the text in that upright orientation, which is the RIGHT-hand side of
the supplied image; I cannot give "line from top of image" for sideways text.

image-002 (tab on first board; four lines, the first and last cut through):
image-002 l.1  ][..]ipine(?) [gap, rubbed] [..]ssiones(?)/[..]tiones(?)
image-002 l.2  [dark, smudged tall capital + 3-4 letters, perhaps "Cap..." or "Exp..."]
               [..]R(?)o su(n)t(?)/sui(?) ho(?) . q(ui)a acuaui[     (written "q" with superscript a, then
               "acuaui" + a minim at the cut edge; "euacuaui[t]" is not excluded)
image-002 l.3  sicut . [tall flourished capital, E or C, with a stroke above]e (con)(?) in
               uuln(er)ib(us)(?) [..]o(?) [..]u[          (the word after "in" is written "uuls/uuln"
               + abbreviation + several compressed letters; very uncertain)
image-002 l.4  [tops cut] ][..]atat(?)[.] uisum(?) siu[   (or "nisum sui")

image-007 (tab on second board; six lines, plus more hidden in the fold below):
image-007 l.1  ][..]ali(?) iudicat(ur)(?) nec ora(?)[.] . tre[
image-007 l.2  uag(?)it(ur)(?)/nog[..] in exiguo(?) a(?) maiori[..](?) [corner folded over]
image-007 l.3  et sp(irit)ualib(us) . ij . art[..]u(m)(?) cura(m)(?) ac lib[..]   (written "sp" + "ualib" with
               mark, then "ij" between points; the middle words are minims with strokes)
image-007 l.4  [..] q(u)i m(ih)i(?) erit(?)/erui(?) poss(et)(?) . uniuigenue(?)[   (last word: a long run
               of minims with g and n; not resolved)
image-007 l.5  [rubbed, small hole] [..]p(er)(?)ac[..]  amb(?)u(?) a(?)c . Rap(?)in[   (a capital R or K with
               a point before it)
image-007 l.6  ][..]is in mic(?)a[..]e in sum(?)mi[..]      (running along the fold; then at least
               three further lines are visible edge-on in the joint: unreadable)

image-012 (spine panel; about 12 lines, pierced by the endband tie-downs and
flaked; read in three passes; right-hand ends run under the sewing support):
image-012 l.1  ][..]mm[..] et iniq(ui)(?)[..] . in eo eo(?) qui[
image-012 l.2  ][..]ic(?) . Recep(?)[..] [flaked] [..]matam(?)
image-012 l.3  ] . vi . factu(?)/iactu(?)  esse  t(?)ialea(?) a[
image-012 l.4  ] [..]nimicor(?)[..] a(?) [flaked]
image-012 l.5  ] Sacra(?)m(en)ta(?) cum(?) [..]
image-012 l.6  ][..] leuior(?)[..]/clerico(rum)(?)  in[..]a[
image-012 l.7  ][..]ix(?)it[..] [..]statur(?) q(ui)a esse(?)[
image-012 l.8  ][..]tur non q(ua)ntit(?)at(?)[..] [..]ma et(?) i[
image-012 l.9  ][..]mus(?) [..]anis . Et a(?)rdet(?)/Exaltet(?)[
image-012 l.10 ][..]a[..]ul[..]  amicit(?)[..]
image-012 l.11 [red paraph or red initial stroke] [..] In q(ui)b(us)(?)[
image-012 l.12 [tops only]
In image-012 I am reasonably confident only of: ". vi ." (a numeral between points)
in l.3, "esse" in l.3, "quia" in l.7, "non" in l.8, ". Et" in l.9, and the red mark
before l.11. Everything else there is a guess at letter shapes.

--- (B) Small-script piece 4 ---
image-005 (tab, first board; 4 line-ends; read turned 90 degrees counter-clockwise):
 ... ][..]a(?) ymn(?)[   /   ][..]tus(?) . vi     - two further lines of minims unread.
image-010 (tab, second board) and image-015 (spine panel): four to ten short line
 segments of 3-6 letters each; the writing on these appears to me to stand the
 other way up relative to piece 1 (uncertain); a thin red line crosses image-015.
 I could not read any word securely. Not transcribed.

LIMITATIONS
- All text is seen as narrow strips cut across the lines (large script) or along
  them (small script); no line is complete at either end. Nothing here is a
  continuous ten-line span; the leaf does not allow it.
- For the large script the letter readings in image-004, image-003 and image-013
  are secure where no (?) is given; image-014 and image-008 are damaged.
- For the small script the hand is clear only on image-002 and image-007, and even
  there the abbreviations are dense; treat every word marked (?) as unverified.
  The spine panel image-012 is abraded and pierced.
- Order of the three parts of each piece (which board is the front) is not
  determinable from these images, so I have not concatenated tab-panel-tab.
- The parts of each strip hidden in the two joints would complete several words.
  Useful additional views: the spine panels photographed square-on in raking
  light at higher magnification, the tabs of piece 1 and 4 photographed upright,
  and the joint gaps opened enough to see the turned text.
